newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan, Uganda resuming diplomatic relations.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Uganda resuming diplomatic relations.

text.p: Sudan and Uganda, responding to Iranian mediation, agreed on Monday to resume diplomatic relations broken in April last year.

"Sudan and Uganda this morning signed an agreement to normalise relations between the two countries, in a culmination of the Iranian initiative undertaken by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani," the official news agency SUNA said.
Uganda broke diplomatic relations with Sudan in April 1995 after an incident in which Sudanese diplomats refused to surrender a cache of weapons to Ugandan soldiers.

Relations have also been strained over allegations that Sudan is helping the rebel Lord's Resistance Army in northern Uganda and that Uganda is supporting the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) in southern Sudan.

The Sudanese agency said the agreement was signed by Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha, Ugandan Foreign Minister Eriya Kategaya and Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, who was in Khartoum with Rafsanjani.
Rafsanjani arrived in Khartoum from the Ugandan capital Kampala on Sunday. On his African tour he has also been to South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.
Uganda's decision to resume relations will be a rare and welcome piece of good news for the Khartoum government.

Sudan has been at odds with most of its neighbours and will face a new round of U.N. sanctions later this year if it fails to convince the U.N. Security Council that it cannot find three men wanted for trying to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa last year.
There was no immediate explanation for Uganda's gesture but the Christian fundamentalist rebels of the Lord's Resistance Army have been especially active recently.

They have been fighting a guerrilla war in the Acholi region of northern Uganda since 1987, ostensibly to overthrow the government of President Yoweri Museveni and rule Uganda according to the Ten Commandments. The war has paralysed life in northern Uganda for long periods.
The Sudanese agency did not mention any deal for the two countries to stop supporting rebel movements on the border.
